Safe and well judged on the main point. The draft treats the Achilles as the headline, drops the quality session and refers Johnny to a physio or sports-med clinician this week, before Thursday. It also sets hard-stop rules for the runs. Volume falls from 31 to about 23 mi plus 40 minutes on the bike or elliptical. The long run drops to 10 mi with no pickup. Easy days are short, flat and capped by heart rate, Wednesday only runs if Tuesday went well, and Monday and Friday stay as rest days. That fits his history of shin splints and his wish for careful mileage. Every day is clear enough to run as written.

The answers are the weak point. Both questions are mostly passed to the physio ("I am not the person to make that call"). The plan does answer question 1 in practice: keep running easy, with stop rules. But question 2 needed some direct warning signs, such as pain getting worse while running, pain at rest or in the morning, swelling, a limp, or pain when hopping. Those would have helped an anxious athlete more than another referral. A 10-mile run on a tender Achilles is borderline, though the stop rules soften it.
